primary_claim: In preliminary experiments with small, non-reasoning-trained models, LLMs show little evidence of tracking or updating beliefs about the final answer during chain-of-thought reasoning, or of anticipating that answer before it is explicitly stated.
contradicts_or_qualifies: Anthropic's finding that Claude anticipates future rhyme words while writing poetry (transformer-circuits.pub attribution graphs)
Shai et al. (arXiv:2405.15943) showing transformers can learn to represent and Bayesian-update beliefs about system state in toy settings
stated_future_work: look into connections to Shai et al.'s work on computational mechanics to find better ways of measuring beliefs during CoT
try running similar experiments with open-weights reasoning models like r1 or its distillations
limitations_stated: prompting on partial CoTs takes the model far outside the state it was in when generating the CoT, so it's unclear how relevant the responses are
there is no ground truth for what the LLM is 'thinking' partway through a CoT to train the linear probes on
linear probes sometimes learned spurious features of the dataset, such as position-dependent answer-letter bias
only examined older and relatively small (<=14B) models with no RL fine-tuning for reasoning
many benchmarks used (BIGBench, CommonsenseQA) have quality issues such as inconsistent formatting and ambiguous questions
quote: I did not find much evidence that LLMs are aware of which answer the CoT will end up picking, or that they track beliefs about the final answer that they update while generating the CoT.
